metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent clicked the system tray icon, used the volume slider in the GNOME system tray menu to drag it all the way to the right (max/100%), then dismissed the menu.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open system tray menu, locate and interact with the volume controls (slider and mute button)
metadata.explanation: Variant requiring muting instead of maximizing volume. The agent uses the same system tray menu (same demonstrated capability). Evaluator runs pactl get-sink-mute and checks for 'Mute: yes'. Initial state has mute disabled so the initial state does not pass.
metadata.task_rationale: Same GNOME system tray interaction family; muting is a sibling action to volume adjustment. Uses existing check_include_exclude metric without custom code.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (vm_command_line) runs 'pactl get-sink-mute @DEFAULT_SINK@', which is the correct PulseAudio command to query mute state of the default audio sink.
The expected output 'Mute: yes' is exactly what pactl returns when the sink is muted, making the expected value semantically correct.
check_include_exclude receives the rules dict directly (via get_rule when expected.type='rule') and accesses rules.get('include', []) correctly — no parameter handling error.
The single instruction requirement (mute the system volume) is fully and exclusively covered by the evaluator — no missing sub-goals.
No postconfig is needed because the getter uses a command-line query, not a UI dialog that could be closed.
Negative control resistance is confirmed: initial state has mute disabled, so the initial state will not pass the evaluator.
